title: Choose the visual world for skyplate
question: The roll dealt Specimen Cabinet. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Every option keeps the same product: a 3D galaxy map, D3 charts, explorer, and source reader.

options.label: Specimen Cabinet
options.lineage: natural-history collection drawers, unit trays, and accession labels
options.thesis: Every file is a catalogued specimen: classified, labeled, and pinned where it was collected.
materials: white unit trays ruled in hairline
a dark glass plate for the galaxy
options.viewport: Gray-blue drawer rail of directories on the left, the dark galaxy plate filling the center with pinned labels, an accession record for the selection on the right, and a row of unit-tray charts below.
options.risk: The museum idea can slide into costume (pins, brass, parchment); it has to stay in the labels and the taxonomy, not in ornament.

raised.raise: One history scrubber remaps every mark at once: the galaxy, every chart, and the explorer all move through time together.
Each directory gets one region geometry, which drives its galaxy hull, label placement, hover, and selection.
Every rule and tray divider is one device pixel, drawn from live layout boxes so it stays crisp at any zoom.
Focusing a drawer lifts its specimens and dims the rest of the collection in every view.

options.label: Geological Survey
options.lineage: USGS and BGS bedrock geology sheets and the chronostratigraphic chart
options.thesis: The codebase as surveyed ground: languages are formations, and history settles as strata.
materials: flat formation fills with letter codes
options.viewport: A stratigraphic column of languages down the left edge that is the legend, filter, and composition chart at once, the galaxy as the map sheet, and history drawn below as sediment layers by language.
options.risk: After the star chart, a map of code is the next most expected move, and formation colors have to be re-stepped to pass the color-blind checks.

options.label: Gate Board
options.lineage: segmented boarding passes and airport departure boards
options.thesis: Watch the codebase rerank: hotspots, owners, and changes listed like departures.
materials: one alert color held on change
options.viewport: A segmented project pass across the top, the galaxy in the center, and a departure board on the right that reorders rows in place when you change the ranking metric.
options.case: Fuses cleanly for audits, because rankings that rerank in place are the whole job, but it says less about structure and taxonomy than the roll does.
options.risk: It can read as a single-leaderboard tool, and the board competes with the map for attention.

options.label: High-Density Mosaic
options.thesis: Everything about the repository on one ruled screen, read by scanning rather than scrolling.
materials: compact gothic sans at small sizes
options.viewport: A two-row nav rail, then a packed mosaic of ruled modules with red tabs, with the galaxy as the largest module among dozens of compact charts and lists.
options.case: Holds product clarity for recurring audits, where density pays off; loses on identification for first-time readers and stakeholders.
options.risk: It overwhelms on first open, and the galaxy shrinks into one module among many.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: One slider morphs the whole grid.
options.viewport: A giant metric readout with a grid of files breathing as one axis moves.
options.case: Developers and stakeholders don't recognize their codebase in a type foundry's world, and it hides the structure.
options.risk: Pure scale contrast leaves no room for dense metrics.
options.kept: One control remaps every mark continuously, so the roll gains a single history scrubber.

options.label: Garden Guide Map
options.lineage: zoo and garden visitor guide maps
options.thesis: Directories as swelling lobes of flat color.
options.viewport: One directory lobe dominates the screen with the others at the coast.
options.case: It's too playful for architecture reviews, and lobes can't carry dense per-file metrics.
options.kept: One geometry drives layout, art, and state, so each directory gets one hull shape used everywhere.

options.label: Centre-Rail Edition
options.thesis: Two text columns around a rail of keys.
options.viewport: A source listing in twin columns with metrics hung in the margin.
options.case: It's a reading world, so it serves only the source view and not the map or the dashboard.
options.kept: Every rule is drawn at one device pixel from live layout.

options.label: Title Card Wall
options.thesis: Rows of directories with files as poster tiles.
options.viewport: Directory rows scrolling sideways, with the focused file expanded.
options.case: Files have no artwork, so the tiles would be empty and the wall says nothing about how files relate.
options.kept: Focus lifts the active set and dims everything else, applied across every view.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark developer-analytics dashboard in the style of GitHub Insights or Grafana, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A sidebar of sections, a KPI row, the galaxy in a large card, and charts in a two-column card grid.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other code-analytics dashboard by design.
